label: <DEL> step of short sequences (L<=4), boosted by certain first tokens
explanation: Fires exclusively at the <DEL> delimiter step (100% of activation mass; never in original or copy phases), on 13% of delimiter steps. Rate falls steeply with sequence length: ~85% of L=3 delimiters, ~38% of L=4, ~7% at L=5, <1% for L>=6; L<=4 holds ~70% of mass. Within a length, it is further modulated by the first original token (the one about to be output): 3, c, 2, z, l, 1, o, q raise rate and magnitude (top examples almost all start with 3), and by the last original token (b, g, y, s, p, f). Top activations: L=3-4 sequences starting with 3, e.g. 3 g g <DEL>. Adding first/last-token conditions reaches F1 ~0.63 but needs ad hoc token lists, so the behavior looks like a graded mix of short length and first-token identity rather than a clean boolean.
